subject: POC sprint backlog: auth handshake, tool-call specs, and streaming behavior
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.t@newline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC sprint backlog: auth handshake, tool-call specs, and streaming behavior

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. I promised to capture the follow-ups for the POC sprint so your engineering team and ours can align on scope and acceptance criteria. Below is a compact recap and the immediate asks we need to close to start the spike next week.

Quick recap of what we covered:
- Target workload: conversational question-answering over internal docs (~20 QPS peak, median seq len 240 tokens)
- Desired features: streaming tokens to UI, structured tool-calling for DB lookups, embeddings for semantic retrieval + reranker
- Security: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for keys in the private deployment

Immediate asks (action owners in parens):
1) Auth handshake: confirm whether you want API-key bearer per-request or OAuth2 client-credentials from your side. If OAuth2, we need client_id + redirect/callback details (Sam).
2) SDK setup: we’ll provide a minimal node/python snippet — what runtime constraints do you have? (Ben)
3) Routing and fallbacks: we proposed an auto-fallback to a smaller model for cost-sensitive routes; need to know which routes are latency-critical vs. cost-critical (Sam/Procurement).
4) Tool-calls: please confirm the shape of your DB lookup payload (fields we should send back and permissions model) so we can define the structured output contract (Vanessa).
5) Streaming semantics: confirm whether you require partial deltas for tokens (client-side incremental merge) or only server-sent final chunks on end-of-response. Also how you expect stop signals handled for mid-stream termination.

Attachments: I’ve attached a first-pass POC checklist and a draft SLA we can start with.

Next steps: if we can get answers to (1),(3),(4),(5) by Thursday EOD, we’ll schedule a 90-minute engineering alignment (spike kickoff) on Monday.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sam Torres <sam.t@newline.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@newline.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC sprint backlog: auth handshake, tool-call specs, and streaming behavior

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline below. Apologies for the long note, wanted to be explicit so your team can prototype correctly.

1) Auth handshake: We prefer OAuth2 client-credentials. We will spin up a client_id / client_secret and run token exchange against our internal auth server. I attached a short spec of our token TTL and rotation policy. We will share the client_id and a test client_secret in a secure vault prior to the spike.

2) SDK runtime constraints: Node 18 (server) and Python 3.11 (worker). We do not support Java or Go in the initial POC.

3) Routing and fallbacks: We have two route types —
  - live-search (UI path, <100ms tail latency SLO)
  - batch-analytics (background, throughput>200 QPS, cost-sensitive)
We want the live-search route pinned to a low-latency model with no auto-fallback to save on quality; background can use fallbacks and aggressive batching.

4) Tool-calls (DB lookup): We will accept a structured JSON input: {"query_id":"string","user_id":"string","context_keys":["string"],"max_results":10}. Response must include: rows:[{id,score,source,excerpt}] plus a status code. We will attach a sample payload.

5) Streaming semantics: We need token-level streaming for live-search (incremental update to UI). For stop signals, the client will send a POST /v1/stop with a request_id; we expect the server to flush partial context and return a truncated final chunk with an "is_truncated":true flag. For background paths we prefer a complete final response only.

Attachments: sample-db-payload.json and oauth-token-policy.pdf

Sam
Principal Engineer, Integrations
NewLine AI
---
Attachment: sample-db-payload.json (application/json)
Attachment: oauth-token-policy.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.t@newline.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jun 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC sprint backlog: auth handshake, tool-call specs, and streaming behavior

Sam —

Appreciate the detailed answers. A few engineering notes and a couple of requests so we can finalize the sample SDK and the request/response contract: 

A) OAuth: Our private deployment expects a short-lived bearer token and will cache token TTLs for up to 60s to avoid token stampedes. Can your token TTL be <= 10 minutes? If not, we’ll add a lightweight refresh shim in the SDK.

B) SDK: we’ll publish a minimal Node + Python repo with two modes: streaming websocket client for live-search and a standard HTTP client for batch-analytics. For the websocket streaming we need to agree on framing: JSON lines where each line is either {"delta":"...","type":"token"} or a control frame {"type":"stop","request_id":"...","is_truncated":true}. Is that acceptable?

C) Structured output / tool-call contract: We can map your DB response to a typed schema and include a reranker endpoint inside the POC. Question: do you need the reranker to be stateful (keep click feedback) or stateless? Stateful implies a small KV for session signals.

D) Tokenization and max_tokens: For live-search we recommend a max_output_tokens=128; for exploratory conversational flows we propose 512. Confirm which ceiling NewLine prefers. Also we’ll instrument token counters on the SDK and emit per-request token usage to your analytics endpoint.

E) Stop behavior: we will implement your POST /v1/stop semantics and include an explicit final chunk with is_truncated true when mid-stream terminated. Note that early stop may drop trailing tool-call completion; we suggest clients call a follow-up sync endpoint to fetch completed tool-call results if needed.

Open asks for you to confirm by Monday so we can land the SDK PR before the spike: token TTL tolerance, desired max_output_tokens for live-search, and whether reranker must be stateful.

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: proposed-sdk-framing.md (text/markdown)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.t@newline.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC sprint backlog: auth handshake, tool-call specs, and streaming behavior

Sam / Ben —

Perfect, thanks for the quick responses. Short readout and next steps so everyone is aligned: 

1) NewLine will provide an OAuth client_id and test credentials in our vault by Monday 2028-07-02 EOD. (Sam)
2) NewLine confirms live-search max_output_tokens = 96 (KPI: <100 token snippets) and background conversational ceiling = 512. (Sam)
3) NewLine prefers reranker to be stateless for the POC — we’ll plan for sessionless scoring. (Sam)
4) Redwood will:
   - Publish initial SDK (Node 18 + Python 3.11) with websocket streaming framing and stop-control shim (Ben) by 2028-07-01.
   - Provide a small test harness that emits token counts and posts usage to your analytics endpoint. (Ben)
   - Update POC checklist + SLA with the agreed token ceilings and streaming contract. (Karthik/Vanessa)

I’ll schedule the 90-minute spike kickoff for Monday 2028-07-04 10:00 PT — invite to follow once calendars confirm. If any of the deadlines above are hard to meet, flag now so we can adjust scope.

Thanks everyone — excited to get started.

Karthik
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
